title_options: Two Agents, One Ollama Server: Why Requests Slow Down
Second Agent Session, Same Server: Where the Wait Comes From
Ollama Concurrency: One Slot, One Queue, Two Slow Sessions
presentation.title_rationale: Selected title front-loads the product (Ollama) and the reader's symptom (requests slow down) in 54 characters, so a developer scanning results knows this is about one shared server process, not about model quality. The mechanism, the 2-vCPU scope and the 2026 measurement date moved into the introduction, description and cover footer instead of being packed into the headline; the old 100-character title buried the shared-server symptom behind 'context and tool calls'. 'Slow down' is a direction claim, not a magnitude claim - no latency figure appears in the title - and the four-slot negative result is not promised there either.
presentation.visual_purpose: Shows the queue the client cannot see: two agent sessions are two HTTP clients against one Ollama process, whose parallel slots decide what runs while the queue holds the rest in arrival order; the client only observes per-request wall time, the sum of queue wait and execution. It is a conceptual schematic grounded in the article's documented defaults and wording, carries no latency or throughput numbers, uses equal-sized bar segments so no magnitude is implied, and its footer marks the scope as a 2-vCPU CPU host with no GPU claim.
presentation.cover_alt: Conceptual diagram: two agent sessions send HTTP requests to one Ollama server process, whose parallel slots decide what runs and whose queue holds the rest in arrival order; the client only sees per-request wall time, the sum of queue wait and execution. Documentation-scoped schematic for a 2-vCPU CPU host, not a measurement chart.
